body.statement: There are fixed constants \(C_0,C_1<\infty\) such that \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal M}P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}(\mathcal E_{n,\alpha})\ge1-\alpha\). On \(\mathcal E_{n,\alpha}\), the Jackson spline approximants to every \(f_x,q_x\) and Carathéodory atomic approximants to \(\phi_1,\phi_2\) belong to \(\Theta_{n,\alpha}\), and their ADRF differs from \(\mu\) by at most \(b_{\mu,n}\) on \(I\). For every realized sample satisfying \(\min_xn_x\ge np_{\min}/2\) and \(\Theta_{n,\alpha}\ne\varnothing\), every \(\theta,\theta^{\prime}\in\Theta_{n,\alpha}\) satisfies \(\|\mu_{\theta}-\mu_{\theta^{\prime}}\|_{L^{\infty}(I)}\le C_0\{K_n^{1/2-\beta}+(\lambda_n/n)^{1/2}\}\le C_1r_n\), whether or not \(\mathcal E_{n,\alpha}\) occurs. For every sample, the clipping rule gives \(0\le W_n\le2B_Y\).
body.justification: This statement isolates the exact coverage event, sieve embedding, nonlinear analytic stability bound, and global clipping bound needed for honest expected width.
body.gap: Capitao-Miniconi, Gassiat, and Lehéricy control an unmarked density in \(L^2\); the present stability problem is a marked quotient in supremum norm with an estimated mixture mass and two unknown asymmetric error factors.
body.consumer: It converts the explicit finite-dimensional confidence set into coverage and a deterministic width bound on the regular count event.

obligation.what_is_open: The constrained-sieve embedding and the quantitative discrete analytic-cocycle modulus at order \(K_n^{1/2-\beta}\) are not established.
obligation.obstruction: Local qualitative identifiability gives no uniform singular-value estimate. The frozen core supplies neither a proved stability inequality for the bilinear grid map nor a specified shape-preserving Jackson construction satisfying every sieve constraint.
obligation.attempted: I proved the simultaneous empirical-transform event with the stated radii and the global clipping bound, then isolated the remaining deterministic inverse inequality. Direct interpolation is insufficient because it does not control the unknown error factors or preserve the nonlinear quotient constraints.
obligation.partial_result:
The confidence-event and clipping portions are derivable.  Conditional on \(n_x\), each complex probability summand has modulus at most one and each marked summand has modulus at most \(B_Y\).  Applying the real bounded-variable exponential inequality to real and imaginary parts gives, when \(n_x>\lambda_n\),
\[
 P\left(\left.|\widehat F_{x,n}-F_x|>2\sqrt{\lambda_n/n_x}\,\right|\,(X_i)_{i=1}^n\right)\le4e^{-\lambda_n},
\]
and the analogous bound for \(G_x\) with radius \(2B_Y\sqrt{\lambda_n/n_x}\).  When \(n_x\le\lambda_n\), the deterministic bounds \(|\widehat F-F|\le2\) and \(|\widehat G-G|\le2B_Y\) apply.  A union bound over both channels, all cells, and \(\mathcal D_n\) costs at most \(8|\mathcal X||\mathcal D_n|e^{-\lambda_n}=\alpha/6\).  Together with \(\mathrm{lem{:}mass\text{-}confidence}\), this proves \(P(\mathcal E_{n,\alpha})\ge1-\alpha/2\), hence the weaker claimed \(1-\alpha\) bound.  Also, every feasible \(\mu_\theta\) lies in \([-B_Y,B_Y]\); the endpoint definition therefore gives \(0\le W_n\le2B_Y\), including the empty-set convention.

The unproved kernel is the uniform quantitative inverse estimate
\[
 \sup_{\theta,\theta'\in\Theta_{n,\alpha}}
 \|\mu_\theta-\mu_{\theta'}\|_{L^\infty(I)}
 \lesssim K_n^{1/2-\beta}+\sqrt{\lambda_n/n}.
\]
Qualitative analytic continuation does not imply this modulus.  A proof must give singular-value bounds for the discrete bilinear cocycle with two unknown atomic error factors and then transfer them through the quotient.  In addition, no shape-preserving Jackson operator has been specified that simultaneously preserves normalization, the lower bound on \(I\), the \(H^\beta\) radii, and \(|q|\le B_Yf\); ordinary Jackson approximation alone establishes none of those feasibility constraints.
